title: Work slice of an encoded snapshot
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet with $k$ work tapes, let a binary code be given for its optional states, and let $s$ be a snapshot of $M$. For each work tape $	au$, the two bits in the work-symbol slice for $	au$ of the encoded snapshot are exactly the two-bit encoding of the symbol on tape $	au$ in $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite binary-alphabet machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes
A binary code for the optional states of $M$
replaced: For every snapshot $s$ and every work tape $\tau$ of a machine with a fixed optional-state binary code, the work slice at $\tau$ of the encoded block of $s$ equals the two-bit encoding of the symbol of $s$ on tape $\tau$.
